subject.title: user-switched model has no fallback chain, causing session deadlock on provider outage

question: Should an exact user-selected model remain strict by default, or should OpenClaw offer a maintainer-approved opt-in policy that allows configured fallback models for that session?
rationale: Current main and its tests intentionally preserve strict user overrides, while the live reports demonstrate an availability cost; choosing between user-selection fidelity and temporary fallback routing is a product and provider-policy decision.

options.title: Keep strict-only behavior
options.body: Preserve the present contract and close or reframe this request as an intentional exact-model-selection policy.

options.title: Approve a resilient opt-in
options.body: Adopt a narrow opt-in policy for user overrides, retaining strict as the default and requiring documented provider/model routing semantics plus focused regression and live failover proof.

options.title: Change the default to resilient
options.body: Treat every user selection as a preference and permit configured fallback candidates without a new setting, accepting the compatibility change for existing exact-model workflows.

recommendation.title: Approve a resilient opt-in
recommendation.body: Adopt a narrow opt-in policy for user overrides, retaining strict as the default and requiring documented provider/model routing semantics plus focused regression and live failover proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is already assigned to osolmaz, and the remaining blocker is policy direction rather than a missing source-level diagnosis.
